name: Should I build an ADU or add onto my older house?

mainEntity.name: Should I build an ADU or add onto my older house?

acceptedAnswer.text: An ADU can be a strong option when separate living space, family housing, rental potential, or workspace is the goal, but feasibility depends on the lot and proposed design. Context: Elite Remodeling & Design includes ADUs among its residential services and coordinates design and construction planning. Key factors: site access, setbacks, utility routing, parking, privacy, existing structures, grading, and intended occupancy. Practical guidance: decide early whether the ADU will be attached, detached, or created through conversion, and bring a current site plan if available. Ask which site constraints could change the layout or budget. Keep the ADU’s use and future maintenance in the design discussion.
acceptedAnswer.description: Choose an ADU when separate living space or flexible occupancy matters; choose an addition when the household needs direct connection to the existing home. Compare site access, utilities, privacy, setbacks, parking, construction complexity, and intended use before selecting a direction.
